title: Atlas and Clock
premise: In the final winter of a devastating continental war, Elodie Oyelaran works as a battlefield nurse in a requisitioned convent hospital, secretly recording in a ledger the names of soldiers, deserters, and civilians that official reports erase. When an unknown woman leaves a six-year-old boy at the hospital door with money and the instruction to forget his face, Elodie recognizes him as the son of a man whose name exists only in her ledger. As evacuation orders arrive and transport berths dwindle to one, Elodie must decide between saving the child, her fellow nurse Marguerite, or the wounded officer who knows too much about the ledger. In the end, Elode gives up her own berth, sends the boy and Marguerite ahead, and burns the ledger after memorizing every name—surviving the war's last days by becoming, at last, one of the remembered rather than the forgotten.
about_author: August Delacroix is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing unclaimed wartime letters in European municipal collections. Atlas and Clock is their second novel, following a widely praised debut about railway porters during the armistice.

chapters.title: The Weight of Names
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Introduces the convent hospital in winter 1917 and Elodie's secret ledger of erased names, begun after a dying soldier was buried as 'Unknown Male.' Emotional beat: quiet defiance born of grief.

chapters.title: Instructions in Chalk
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. A woman leaves a silent boy, Henri, at the door with coins and a note: forget the face. Sister Superior wants him gone by morning. Emotional beat: unease hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: What the Boy Won't Say
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. The young nurse tries to coax Henri to speak; he draws maps instead—streets no one recognizes. Elodie notices the drawings match a dead soldier's hometown. Emotional beat: tenderness shadowed by dread.

chapters.title: The Ledger Grows Heavy
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. A raid on the hospital for deserters forces Elodie to hide both patients and the ledger inside the chapel crypt. Emotional beat: terror of discovery, first taste of real risk.

chapters.title: Officer Verrec
chapters.summary: Verrec's POV. A convalescing intelligence officer arrives, sharp-eyed and courteous, asking questions about missing personnel files. He notices Elodie's careful handwriting. Emotional beat: cat-and-mouse politeness.

chapters.title: Atlas Without Borders
chapters.summary: Henri's POV (rendered close-third). The boy finally speaks, revealing his father was executed as a deserter—the first name in Elodie's ledger. Emotional beat: the child's loneliness mirroring Elodie's.

chapters.title: The Clock in the Bell Tower
chapters.summary: Sister Béatrice's POV. The convent's ancient clock stops; the Mother Superior calls it an omen. Rumors arrive that the front is collapsing and evacuation may come within weeks. Emotional beat: time becoming an antagonist.

chapters.title: A Bargain in the Dispensary
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Verrec offers protection from the raids in exchange for the ledger's names—he claims he wants to notify families. Elodie neither refuses nor agrees. Emotional beat: temptation wearing a kind face.

chapters.title: Marguerite's Letter
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. She confesses she has been writing to a prisoner-of-war camp and asks Elodie to add her brother's name to the ledger. Their friendship deepens into chosen family. Emotional beat: belonging found in shared secrets.

chapters.title: The Evacuation Order
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Official orders arrive: the hospital will be evacuated in twelve days. One military truck, limited berths, priority given to officers. Emotional beat: the abstract war turning concrete and cruel.

chapters.title: Counting Berths
chapters.summary: Sister Béatrice's POV. The nuns debate who qualifies: the wounded, the children, the staff. Henri has no papers; officially he does not exist. Emotional beat: bureaucracy as violence.

chapters.title: What Verrec Knows
chapters.summary: Verrec's POV. He reveals he has traced Henri's father—and that the execution order bore a signature connected to his own unit. His guilt reframes his interest in the ledger. Emotional beat: a man drowning in complicity.

chapters.title: Night of the Long Roll Call
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. A final inspection demands names for every soul in the convent. Elodie reads aloud from memory, giving the dead names and Henri a false one. Emotional beat: the ledger spoken as liturgy.

chapters.title: The Face She Was Told to Forget
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Marguerite realizes the woman who left Henri was seen again in the village—alive, searching, afraid. Hope and danger arrive together. Emotional beat: the past refusing to stay buried.

chapters.title: Three Names, One Seat
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. The arithmetic becomes brutal: one berth remains beyond the assigned wounded. Henri, Marguerite, or Elodie herself. Verrec can secure one name on the list—for a price. Emotional beat: love measured against survival.

chapters.title: The Price Named Aloud
chapters.summary: Verrec's POV. Verrec asks not for the ledger but for Elodie to testify that he tried to save the boy's father—a lie to carry into peacetime. Elodie must weigh truth against mercy. Emotional beat: the cost of absolution.

chapters.title: Burning the Midnight Page
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Elodie memorizes all three hundred and eleven names, then feeds the ledger page by page into the boiler. If it cannot leave, it will live in her. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into vow.

chapters.title: The Truck at Dawn
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs interwoven. Loading day: shelling nears the town, the clock tower takes a hit, and the convoy schedule collapses into chaos. Emotional beat: panic where order should be.

chapters.title: The Last Berth
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. At the truck, Elodie puts Henri aboard in Marguerite's care and steps back, surrendering her seat. Verrec, watching, silently gives up his own place beside them. Emotional beat: sacrifice without ceremony.

chapters.title: Ash and Snowfall
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Left behind as the town falls, Elodie shelters in the ruined chapel with Sister Béatrice, reciting names through the night like a rosary. Emotional beat: stillness inside catastrophe.

chapters.title: Armistice Morning
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. In the safe city, Henri speaks his father's full name aloud for the first time; Marguerite writes it down. Word comes that survivors are walking out of the fallen zone. Emotional beat: fragile, disbelieving hope.

chapters.title: Atlas and Clock
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Weeks later, Elodie arrives at Marguerite's door carrying nothing but a coat and three hundred and eleven names held in memory. Henri runs to meet her. Emotional beat: homecoming—not to a place, but to the people who remember you.
